title: X-Scientist: A Recursive Self-Improving Agentic AI Platform for Drug Discovery | Xaira Therapeutics
content: We introduce X-Scientist, Xaira’s agentic AI platform for drug discovery and design. X-Scientist brings together frontier language models, biological tools, Xaira’s internal datasets, and our proprietary models to support research spanning mechanistic investigation, target identification, therapeutic design, and analysis and experimental planning. X-Scientist serves as an AI co-scientist across the full scope of drug discovery, working alongside researchers to investigate complex questions, execute computational workflows, and refine scientific understanding as new evidence emerges. By connecting these capabilities with experimental research, X-Scientist helps translate Xaira’s advances in AI and biology into therapeutic programs, advancing our mission to discover and develop new medicines for patients. We evaluated the X-Scientist harness on public scientific benchmarks. On DrugDiscoveryBench [1] and the life sciences subset of Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 [2] , X-Scientist outperformed other tested configurations. We experimentally tested X-Scientist-nominated genetic perturbations in TGF-β–treated liver cells, achieving a hit rate comparable to human curation and identifying perturbations of both canonical and non-canonical genes that reversed the TGF-β response, with nominations generated approximately 10× faster than human curation. These results provide initial evidence that X-Scientist can perform complex scientific tasks, integrate specialized biological models into target discovery research, and accelerate the pace of discovery. The next phase of X-Scientist is to connect scientific reasoning with automated experimentation. By linking proposed experiments to lab execution and feeding results back into the system, we aim to build a continuous cycle of hypothesis, experiment, and analysis. Each result will inform what to investigate next, and scientists will guide the decisions that most need their expertise. We’ll share more soon about X-Automate, our AI robotics platform, and how we’re connecting it with X-Scientist to bring this cycle into the lab. Large language models (LLMs) are already contributing to protein design and experimentally tested biological discoveries [ 3 , 4, 5 ]. Applying these capabilities to drug discovery requires a harness – a system that connects LLMs to the practical work of science. The harness lets LLMs call software tools and programs and work on a task for increasingly long periods without human intervention. Our design principle is to build the X-Scientist harness around three components that Xaira can develop and continually improve: X-Scientist is a multi-agent harness that separates coordination and verification from task execution. A lead agent directs the investigation, delegates tasks, and evaluates the evidence returned by persistent worker agents. Workers use data, tools, compute, and scientific models to produce findings with supporting evidence. A dynamic task graph records the evolving plan and dependencies and serves as working memory to guide subsequent steps as new findings emerge. (Figure 1) Figure 1. X-Scientist agent architecture. Research questions progress through an iterative cycle of planning, execution, and verification, supported by data, tools, and scientific models. X-Scientist combines a broad range of custom bioinformatics and scientific analysis tools with Xaira’s proprietary data and internal models, including X-Cell (]target identification), X-Design (molecular design), and X-Patient (patient stratification). APIs and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers connect these resources to the harness, allowing agents to combine established scientific methods with Xaira’s specialized capabilities within the same investigation. Integrating our internal models requires more than making predictions available. A tailored interpretation layer for each model captures what its outputs represent, how biological and experimental context affects their meaning, and which conclusions they support. X-Scientist incorporates dynamic task graphs that evolve with the scientific task and evidence. The lead agent constructs an initial graph with stages suited to the research question and delegates execution to a worker. The worker maintains the graph and consults the lead after each stage, sharing findings and the current graph state. The lead agent then decides whether to continue, explore alternatives with additional agents, or revise the remaining work. Separating coordination from execution makes the scientific decisions within this process an explicit target for improvement. We retain completed graphs to examine which strategies yielded useful evidence and where effort failed to resolve uncertainty. These records let us study and refine how the lead selects analyses, allocates effort, and requests verification while holding task execution capabilities fixed.
